label: rhizophore
parent: is_a plant axis (PO_0025004); part_of sporophyte shoot system
definition: A leafless, usually unbranched axis that arises at a branching point of the stem in Selaginella and grows towards the substrate, where it produces roots at its tip.
reason: A distinct organ of Selaginella (spikemosses), described in five floras with length, diameter, hairiness and colour. PO has no class for it. Scientists still argue whether it is a root or a shoot, so the neutral parent 'plant axis' is the safe choice. Propose to PO upstream.

Narrower: a strand is a separate portion of sclerenchyma (a tissue of hard, thick-walled cells) seen in leaf cross-sections. Counts ('3 strands', 'few to c. 50') count these portions, as in pattern 03.

target: plant cell (PO_0009002) part of costa (PO_0030072), pattern 12
reason: These are the cells of the moss leaf midrib (the costa), described by shape and as abaxial or adaxial. They are a cell type in a part that already has a class, so the 'part of a qualified whole' pattern covers them; 'abaxial' and 'adaxial' are surface context words.

target: flower (PO_0009046) with bearer state fertile (PATO_0000955), pattern 04
reason: A floret is a flower (rule C261), and 'fertile' is already a context word that sets the bearer's state, with floret in its list. Spikelet floret (PO_0009082) is the narrower class where the flora is about grasses.

target: corolla lobe (FLOPO_0986006) part of disk flower (PO_0025332), pattern 12
reason: In Asteraceae, 'disk lobes' are the corolla lobes of the disk florets. Both classes exist, so the whole they belong to can be stated with pattern 12.
A piece of a count ('setae 1-2 per perichaetium'), like 'per node' and 'per axil', which the previous review rejected. The part being counted is the seta; the perichaetium is only the unit.

target: plant organ base (FLOPO_0985024) part of style (PO_0009074), pattern 12
reason: The base region of the style, for example the persistent tubercle in Cyperaceae. Base is a region the patterns can already express. Where a flora says 'stylopodium' (Apiaceae), use stylopodium (FLOPO_0986022).

A substance, and a general word covering latex, resin, gum and sap. The specific words already have classes: plant latex (FLOPO_0980431), plant resin (PO_0025603), plant sap (PO_0025538). Ground those words, not 'exudate'.

label: column foot
parent: is_a cardinal organ part (PO_0025001); part_of gynostemium (FLOPO_0986015)
definition: A forward extension of the base of the column (gynostemium) of an orchid flower, to which the lateral sepals and the lip are often attached, together forming a mentum.
reason: A real structure in many orchids (Dendrobium, Bulbophyllum, Eria) with its own length, curvature and free part, in five floras. It is an extension rather than just the base of the column, so 'base' would not fit. It sits next to the existing FLOPO classes mentum and gynostemium, so keep it in FLOPO with those orchid classes.

target: plant cell (PO_0009002) part of non-vascular leaf (PO_0025075), pattern 12
reason: These are the cells of moss leaf blades (hexagonal, hyaline, thickened walls). Cell plus the leaf it belongs to gives the meaning; 'cell' alone was rejected in the previous review as too general.

Two different structures share this name. In mosses it is the swollen capsule base (a synonym of sporangium base, PO_0030040). In Pinus it is the exposed thickened end of the cone scale (rhombic, keeled, pyramidal, recurved, as in the examples). It cannot be grounded without knowing which group the flora covers.

target: sepal (PO_0009031) with bearer position lateral, pattern 04 (position value pending)
reason: Narrower: a sepal in the lateral position (orchids, Polygalaceae, Balsaminaceae). Pattern 04 says lateral has no value class yet and five position values are planned. Use the lateral value once it exists; until then the bearer is sepal.
Exact: the frame left between the valves of a Brassicaceae fruit after they fall. The examples are fruit states (persistent, glabrous).

label: perichaetium
definition: The group of modified leaves (perichaetal bracts) together with the archegonia they surround, at the female sex organ site of a moss or liverwort gametophyte.
reason: PO has perichaetal bract (PO_0030030) but not the whole cluster. Floras describe the cluster as terminal or lateral, small, numerous or convolute, and count setae per perichaetium. Propose to PO upstream next to perichaetal bract.

target: bract margin (PO_0025011) part of involucral bract (PO_0009045), pattern 12
reason: Phyllary is a narrow synonym of involucral bract (rule C250), and bract margin exists. Restrict it to the involucral bract with pattern 12.

target: leaflet (PO_0020049) with bearer state terminal (PATO_0002476), pattern 04
reason: 'terminal' is already a context word that sets the bearer's state, with leaflet in its list. Pattern 04 uses 'terminal leaflet' as its example. Apex and base statements then go to leaflet apex and base (FLOPO_0986000, FLOPO_0986001).

Exact: 'sporangium neck' is a PO synonym of sporangium base, and the examples are moss capsule descriptions (wrinkled, tapering). Bare 'neck' was rejected before; this two-word form says which organ it belongs to.
Exact: 'sporangium urn' is a PO synonym. In moss floras the urn is the spore-bearing part of the capsule.

target: plant cell (PO_0009002) part of phyllome margin (PO_0025018), pattern 12
reason: The rows of cells along the edge of moss leaves. Cell plus the margin it belongs to gives the meaning. Phyllome margin is the safe parent because these are non-vascular leaves; leaf margin (PO_0020128) is for vascular leaves.
Exact: 'cone scale' is a PO synonym of megasporophyll. The examples (woody, flattened, insides reddish brown) are scales of seed cones.
An adjective meaning 'bearing appendages', not a part. The appendage itself is a general word that needs its organ, and the previous review rejected 'appendaged' the same way.
A piece of a count from Anthurium spadix descriptions ('4-6 flowers visible in the alternate spiral'). It is a way of counting flowers along a spiral, not a structure; 'spiral' was rejected before.
A piece of a count from Anthurium spadix descriptions ('7-11 flowers visible in principal spiral'). It is a counting convention, not a structure.

Close to exact: in compound-leaf families (Meliaceae, Sapindaceae, Burseraceae) 'leaf axis' is the central axis, the rachis, and is described by hairiness and a channel. Some floras also count the petiole as part of it, so it is slightly broader.
A piece of a count ('2-3 rows of cells' in a border or lamina, as in Fissidens). The bearer is the border or lamina named nearby, and 'cell' alone was rejected before.
Exact: the same structure as the FLOPO staminal tube (fused filaments, as in Meliaceae and Malvaceae). Only the label had no bearer rule.
Exact: 'arista' is a PO synonym of awn, and flora_counted_parts already maps 'aristate' to awn. Counts follow pattern 03.

A general part that needs its organ, like 'lateral lobe' in the previous review. 'Primary' gives a level of division that has no value class. It is mostly leaf lobes but also lobes of other organs. The flora's own organ word should carry the bearer, with leaf lamina lobe (PO_0025517) where it is a leaf.

Narrower: an underleaf (amphigastrium) is the row of ventral leaves of a leafy liverwort, a kind of non-vascular leaf. A FLOPO subclass could come later if floras compare underleaves with lateral leaves.

Narrower or related: in cacti and Thymelaeaceae (tubercles, areole hairs and large sizes in the examples) the 'flower tube' is the floral cup, a hypanthium, and PO lists 'floral cup' as a synonym. Where a flora clearly means a fused perianth, use perianth tube (FLOPO_0986010) instead.
